title: Three Seasons and One Short Bow
subtitle: 人际交往 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·良好的人际关系与人际交往）
meta: 主题语境：人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·良好的人际关系与人际交往）　|　核心词汇：gentleman　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 gentleman 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the porter ① thanked a gentleman that no passenger in the hall would have described, and he said the thanking was the whole of the season. The ② gentleman, meaning the man himself and not the coat, ran three seasons and stayed undescribed in the book; a gentleman, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ gentleman in that hall had the same short bow beside it, and the ④ gentleman at the far window, meaning the one they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A gentleman, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the porter said the describing is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the gentleman was the whole of the matter, meaning the courtesy and not the man. The ⑥ gentleman, meaning the courtesy and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; gentleman, he said, is either something you thank or the only word that means both a man and a courtesy. He said the courtesy is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ gentleman had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short bow. The ⑧ gentleman of the whole thing, the porter wrote in November, was one hall and three seasons of describing; gentleman, he said, is either the one at the far window or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ gentleman I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1965 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ gentleman, my mother said in 1967, is the only one that improves by being described; every gentleman, she said, is a courtesy that has agreed to look like a man. She said the courtesy was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 绅士；先生（指大厅里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 绅士；先生（指那个人本人，与外套相对）
C. 固定搭配：thank a gentleman 向一位绅士道谢
D. n. 绅士（指留给孩子们仿效的那一位）
E. n. 绅士风度（抽象总称，指一间大厅的绅士之事）
F. n. 绅士（指方案里写到、被记录过的那一位）
G. n. 君子；有教养的人（指一件事里人人都敬却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 教养（抽象总称，指人人都敬却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: thanked a gentleman that no passenger in the hall would have described
The gentleman, meaning the man himself and not the coat
the gentleman at the far window
the gentleman was the whole of the matter
the gentleman had become a line in a plan
The gentleman of the whole thing
A gentleman, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: thank a gentleman 意为“向一位绅士道谢”，1959 年那位门房向大厅里没有一位旅客肯描述的一位绅士道了谢。
gentleman 意为“绅士、先生”，指那个人本人而不是外套，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被描述。
gentleman 意为“绅士、先生”，指大厅里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一次矮矮的鞠躬。
gentleman 意为“绅士”，指最远那扇窗边留给孩子们仿效的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
gentleman 意为“君子、有教养的人”，指一件事里人人都敬却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位君子就是那件事的全部。
gentleman 意为“教养”，指人人都敬却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位绅士，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
gentleman 意为“绅士”，指方案里写到、被记录过的那一位，到 1963 年这一位成了方案里的一行。
gentleman 意为“绅士风度”，门房十一月写道，整件事的绅士之事是一间大厅和三个季度的描述。
gentleman 意为“绅士”，我记得的是方案里描述过的那一位，1965 年离开了，至今仍被说成大厅里最安静的一位。
gentleman 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，一位绅士是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
